function.name: multiple_sequence_alignment
function.description: Obtain a set of nucleotide sequences in FASTA format (DNA) or amino acid sequences (proteins) for multiple sequence alignment. The multiple_sequence_alignment process performs alignment of all input sequences using one or more global alignment algorithms (such as ClustalW, MUSCLE, or MAFFT). Global alignment algorithms take into account sequence similarity, insertions and deletions (gaps), and conserved regions to generate a comprehensive multiple sequence alignment result. The alignment quality is evaluated, with a focus on identifying and highlighting highly conserved regions and important variation sites. The output of the multiple sequence alignment includes a URL for visualizing the alignment result, which can be displayed using Markdown format (e.g., '![](url)') and an aligned matrix, where each row represents an amino acid sequence and each column corresponds to the aligned amino acids at the same position across all sequences.

fasta_text.description: FASTA format consists of nucleotide sequences (DNA) composed of 'A', 'T', 'C', and 'G', or amino acid sequences (protein). If only the sequences are provided without description lines, the description lines will be automatically assigned as '>seq1', '>seq2', and so on by default

function.name: gene_function_annotation
function.description: This function receives a set of user-provided DNA nucleotide sequences or protein amino acid sequences in FASTA format, which are used to perform sequence alignment against all type II polyketide nucleotide or amino acid sequences stored in the database. The type II polyketide information is already embedded in the function code, so only the user input sequences are required. The function is capable of identifying and predicting functionally conserved regions, such as gene functional domains and active sites, to assist in gene and protein function annotation. It primarily uses bitscore and identity to determine which database sequence is most similar to the input sequence, thereby providing functional annotation information. The output table includes the following columns: input sequence, matched sequence, alignment length, identity, bitscore, and gene annotation.

type.description: User inputs the sequence type: DNA (sequences composed of A, T, C, and G) or protein (sequences composed of 20 letters representing amino acids).

function.name: pubchem
function.description: Obtain a compound name to query the PubChem database and retrieve information about the compound. The returned compound information may be irrelevant, so a secondary filtering step based on the compound_name is required to ensure relevance.

compound_name.description: compound name derived from the user's query

function.name: ask_for_help
function.description: Submit a request, and a human assistant can help fulfill any additional tasks that require manual intervention—such as submitting file contents, providing results from physical experiments, and other similar needs.
